findings.description: The cycle guard (`seen` set of exception ids) was removed from the `__cause__` traversal loop. A circular `__cause__` chain now makes the `while exc is not None` loop run forever.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an exception whose `__cause__` chain loops back on itself (e.g. `a.__cause__ = b; b.__cause__ = a`, or `e.__cause__ = e`), with none of the exceptions matching `exception_cause_types`. Mechanism: no visited check remains, so `exc = exc.__cause__` cycles indefinitely. Impact: the retry predicate hangs, which blocks the retrying call. Python does not forbid such cycles when `__cause__` is assigned manually.
